notes.title: Coming Early 2021
notes.content:
Hi there: Ben here, swinging by with an update on the development of Slumber Clause: Episode I.

We care about this game deeply, but it's something we're unfortunately hammering away at between other projects that keep the lights on.

We want to make Slumber Clause super weird and unique in the video game narrative space. But in order to do it right, it is taking time. More time than we initially anticipated.

It's looking like Episode I will be ready in early 2021. Working towards a release in the new year will give us more time to write, revise, and make sure the episode is polished. 

The plan remains for us to do an episodic release of Slumber Clause under the banner of Early Access. We've nailed down a pricing structure and updated the store page accordingly, complete with a nifty animated graphic. If you are a particularly budget conscious game player who is interested in the project, the best time to buy in will be after Episode I comes out but before Episode II.

When you purchase the game early, you'll automatically get future episodes as they are released. This means if you buy Slumber Clause when Episode I comes out, the entire game will cost $3.99 USD, but you'll only have access to the first episode initially.

Buying the game early not only saves you a hefty chunk of cash but helps us better manage development costs as we continue to work on the game's other planned episodes. 

Thank you for your patience as we plug away over here. It's sure been 2020. 

Here's to the new year!

<3, 
Ben

notes.title: Slumber Clause Initial Release Delayed
notes.content:
Today I made the difficult decision to postpone the initial release of [i]Slumber Clause[/i].

Our tiny development team of three was pushing to release Episode I into Early Access in time for Halloween 2020, a pretty ideal time to introduce a new weird, narrative horror game into the world. 

Sadly, the Summer of Coronavirus has been a parade of speed bumps and gear wrenches as I juggle AAA writing commitments with indie passion projects like [i]Slumber Clause[/i]. 

[i]Slumber Clause[/i] is a game I've wanted to make for years—and I want to make sure it is as good as it can be. 

Releasing the game episodically through an early access model is meant to help on this front, as episodic + early access supports the game's ongoing development financially, while also providing us with essential player feedback as we squash bugs, polish the writing, and add new episodes.

Our initial release still needs to be pretty rad, though. And to hit that bar of pretty rad, I need more time to write and test. 

Basically, I don't want to rush this thing. :(

So for now, [i]Slumber Clause[/i]'s Ep. 1 release date is sitting at the ultra-vague date of "2020." I'm flirting with the idea of releasing it when it's ready, setting it live with little warning, "when you least expect it." Whether we go this route or announce a new specific date, you'll be the first to know by wishlisting the game and/or [url=twitter.com/copychaser]following us on Twitter.[/url]

Thank you for your patience, and for your support of Copychaser's weird little games. 

<3
Ben

notes.title: Last Chance to Play Demo
notes.content:
Thanks everyone for trying out the prologue for [i]Slumber Clause[/i]. 

The timed demo was created as part of the Steam Games Festival: Summer Edition. The idea was for the festival demos to go away when the event ended. 

We figured it would be good for the prologue to stick around for a while longer, so our demo is instead set to expire on June 26. 

If you haven't played the demo yet, be sure to play this week! And if you have any comments or feedback on our prologue, please post your thoughts in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/883240/discussions/][i]Slumber Clause [/i]Steam forums[/url].

Halloween is scary close, and a bigger, better prologue will be included with Episode I of the main game. 

We'll have more news on [i]Slumber Clause[/i] in the weeks and months ahead!

👁❤️👻,
Ben

notes.title: Introducing: Slumber Clause
notes.content:
Hi there. My name is Ben Gelinas. I'm a video game writer and designer who works in both AAA and indie spheres. 

Under my Copychaser Games label, I've released one indie game to date: the whole horror conversation sim [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/746400/Speed_Dating_for_Ghosts/][i]Speed Dating for Ghosts[/i][/url].

On the AAA side, my credits include [i]Dragon Age: Inquisition, Mass Effect 3, Mass Effect Andromeda[/i], and, most recently, Remedy Games' new weird action adventure [i]Control[/i].

Working on [i]Control [/i]got me into the New Weird genre of fiction in a big way. I wanted to write my own narrative take on the burgeoning genre. Combine that with a long-held love of old school text adventures and you get...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38052361/cc9b2c112d33379d5ca037864e86d2ad672744fd.png[/img]

Slumber Clause is way more than a throwback to classic text adventures, with modern choice and narrative mechanics piled on top to create an immersive, detailed experience that should appeal to fans of adventure games and BioWare-style choices and characters alike. 

The game is extremely, totally, absolutely focused on story.

You play as a recently-widowed paramedic mom battling a mean case of sleep paralysis. When you're not trying to hold your waking life together, you're navigating surreal dreams of unspeakable beauty and endless possibilities that always seem to end in tragedy.

All the while, a hooded figure stalks you. Collect clues to discover who they are and what they want.

You can read more about the game and demo the prologue for free here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/883240/Slumber_Clause/

Slumber Clause may not be much to look at yet. It's still being made. But if you are interested in where it's going and what it could become, please consider wishlisting my game. I'll be releasing it episodically using Steam's Early Access feature, so early supporters will get the best deal. <3

For those new to my work, thank you for reading all this. 

If you already like Speed Dating for Ghosts, just thank you. A lot. The massive support we've received for our weird little ghosts encouraged me to make more weird games that aren't like anything else out there, because I now know there's an audience of rad people who might want to play them.

👁❤️👻,
Ben
